hello.note: The h is silent. Buenos días, buenas tardes and buenas noches change with the time of day

goodbye.note: Hasta luego (AH-stah LWEH-goh) means see you later

thank-you.note: Muchas gracias (MOO-chahs) means thank you very much

yes.note: The accent mark tells it apart from si, meaning if

excuse-me.note: Con permiso (kohn pair-MEE-soh) when you need to get past someone. Disculpe (dees-KOOL-peh) gets a waiter's attention

my-name.note: Literally "I call myself". The audio uses Peter as the example name

speak-slowly.note: Hable is the polite (usted) form of speak

repeat.note: Puede means can you, in the polite form

speak-english.note: Habla is the polite form of you speak

hundred.note: Exactly 100. For 101 to 199 it becomes ciento

how-much.note: For more than one item say ¿Cuánto cuestan? (KWEHS-tahn)

would-like.note: The polite way to say I would like. Quisiera un café = I'd like a coffee. The audio uses un café as the example

i-want.note: More direct than quisiera. The audio uses esto (this) as the example

do-you-have.note: Put the item in the gap. The audio uses agua (water) as the example

discount.note: Haggling is normal at markets, not in shops

card.note: The j is a breathy h, as in loch

reservation.note: In Spain it is una reserva

checkout-time.say: ah keh OH-rah ehs lah sah-LEE-dah
checkout-time.note: Salida means exit, and is the check-out time

wifi.say: kwahl ehs lah kohn-trah-SEH-nyah dehl WEE-fee
wifi.note: The ñ sounds like ny in canyon

toilet.note: "¿Dónde está …?" means "where is …?" for anything. In Spain you may also see servicios or aseos

bus.note: Also just bus. In Mexico a city bus is often camión

bus-station.note: Terminal de autobuses (tehr-mee-NAHL) is also very common

where-train-station.say: DOHN-deh eh-STAH lah ehs-tah-SYOHN deh trehn

where-bus-station.say: DOHN-deh eh-STAH lah ehs-tah-SYOHN deh ow-toh-BOO-sehs

which-train.note: Swap in any city; the audio uses Hanói (ah-NOY) as the example

buy-ticket.note: Boleto in Latin America; billete (bee-YEH-teh) in Spain

two-tickets.note: The audio uses Hanói as the example city

trip-length.note: The audio uses Hanói as the example city

delicious.note: ¡Qué rico! (keh REE-koh) is the casual version

allergic.note: Women say alérgica (ah-LEHR-hee-kah). Add the food: mariscos (seafood), nueces (nuts), huevo (egg). The audio uses mariscos as the example

love-dish.note: Me encanta means I love it, and works for food, music and places

what-called.note: Point at the dish or item

table-for-two.text: Una mesa para dos, por favor
table-for-two.say: OO-nah MEH-sah PAH-rah dohs por fah-BOR
table-for-two.note: For more people use tres (3) or cuatro (4) instead of dos

beer.text: Una botella de cerveza, por favor
beer.note: Una cerveza alone is the usual order

coffee.note: Café con leche (kohn LEH-cheh) is coffee with milk; café solo is black

tea.note: The accent mark tells it apart from te, meaning you

water.note: Agua sin gas is still water, and con gas is sparkling
